question: What did Kestrel Robotics say about Tray.io?

resolution.read_instruction: Extract every statement about Tray.io (including Tray, and any comparison or competing-vendor mention) made by the customer or prospect or OrbitFlow staff in this call, quoting the speaker's context and any opinions, reasons, or evaluation outcomes stated.
assumptions: Kestrel Robotics is a cold call (CALL-020), so call_types left empty since the question names the company directly.
Tray.io is treated as a competitor or third-party tool mentioned in the call; no catalogue match is needed for it.

findings.speaker: Rafael Santos
findings.quote: We're three weeks into evaluating Tray.io. Your name came up on a list and got crossed off.
findings.context: Rafael said OrbitFlow's name came up on a list of vendors and was crossed off; Kestrel is three weeks into evaluating Tray.io. — Opening context of the evaluation; Tray.io is the vendor currently under evaluation, and OrbitFlow was dropped earlier.

findings.speaker: Rafael Santos
findings.quote: Well. Genuinely well. Their team's been good.
findings.context: Rafael says the Tray evaluation is going well and that Tray's team has been good. — Asked how the Tray evaluation is going; positive sentiment about Tray.

findings.speaker: Leo Grant
findings.quote: I'm not going to tell you Tray is bad. It isn't. We lose to them and we beat them and it usually comes down to fit rather than quality.
findings.context: OrbitFlow staff say they are not going to tell the customer Tray is bad; Tray is a good product and the two vendors usually win or lose on fit rather than quality. — Leo declining to disparage Tray while arguing OrbitFlow is a third horse late in the process.

findings.speaker: Leo Grant
findings.quote: Three weeks in, with a decision coming, I'd be the third horse in a two-horse race, and that's usually a waste of everyone's time.
findings.context: Leo says a third vendor three weeks into a two-horse race would be a waste of time for everyone. — Leo argues against joining the late-stage Tray evaluation.

findings.speaker: Rafael Santos
findings.quote: Tray don't have a connector and we're looking at building against its API, which our one back-end developer estimates at three weeks.
findings.context: Rafael says the one problem in the Tray evaluation is the ERP: Tray has no connector for their niche mid-market manufacturing ERP, so they would build against its API, estimated at three weeks by the developer and, per Rafael, really six. — Only evaluation issue the customer raised regarding Tray.

findings.speaker: Leo Grant
findings.quote: there's a good chance we don't have a connector either.
findings.context: Leo concedes OrbitFlow likely has no native connector for the ERP either, so there is no advantage over Tray on that point. — Leo conceding a comparison point against his own product; no advantage on the ERP connector specifically.

findings.speaker: Leo Grant
findings.quote: Run it against Tray — I mean that, run it against Tray, you're three weeks in and it costs you nothing.
findings.context: Leo suggests testing whether operations staff can change the process without the developer, and says to run that test against Tray, with Rafael saying Tray passing would be a reason to buy it. — Leo recommends the customer test Tray; he says it costs nothing and would be a good decision if Tray passes.

findings.speaker: Rafael Santos
findings.quote: We've got a decision date and I'm not moving it.
findings.context: Rafael says Kestrel will not restart the evaluation and has a fixed decision date in mid-October, with Tray the likely choice. — Customer stating the evaluation timeline; Leo's question about a vendor-agnostic call implies Tray is likely the pick.

rejected_findings.claim: Leo's reading is that Kestrel will likely go with Tray, which is the inferred outcome of the evaluation.
rejected_findings.quote: You'd do that knowing we'll probably go with Tray?
rejected_findings.speaker: Leo Grant
rejected_findings.reason: speaker mismatch or ambiguous attribution (reader said Leo Grant)

draft.answer: Kestrel Robotics' COO Rafael Santos said they are three weeks into evaluating Tray.io and that it is going well [C1]. His one issue is that Tray has no connector for their ERP [C2]. He said the decision date is fixed and Tray looks like the likely pick [C3]. OrbitFlow's Leo Grant declined to disparage Tray [C4] and conceded OrbitFlow likely has no ERP connector either [C5].

claims.text: Rafael Santos (COO) said Kestrel is three weeks into evaluating Tray.io, and that OrbitFlow's name came up on a vendor list and was crossed off.
Rafael said the Tray evaluation is going 'genuinely well' and that Tray's team has been good.

Rafael's one problem with Tray is that it has no connector for their niche mid-market manufacturing ERP. Kestrel would build against the ERP's API, which their one back-end developer estimates at three weeks (Rafael says really six).

Rafael said Kestrel has a fixed decision date in mid-October and will not move it or restart the evaluation. Tray appears to be the likely choice, though this is implied by Leo's question rather than stated outright.

Leo Grant (OrbitFlow AE) said Tray is not bad, that OrbitFlow sometimes wins and sometimes loses to it, and that it usually comes down to fit. He said OrbitFlow would be a third horse in a two-horse race, a waste of everyone's time.
Leo conceded OrbitFlow likely has no native connector for the ERP either, so it has no advantage over Tray on that point.

Leo suggested Kestrel test whether operations staff can change the process without the developer, and run that test against Tray. Per the finding summary, Rafael said Tray passing would be a reason to buy it.

not_covered: Tray.io pricing, features beyond the ERP connector gap, and the exact decision date were not stated in the findings.
assumptions: Tray.io is treated as a competitor evaluated by Kestrel.
